cards.text: Last time, Saul told David, "May you be blessed, David my son." Then he went home (1 Samuel 26:25). But I don't think David's unpacking his bags just yet, friend, because he says to himself, "One of these days now I will be swept away by the hand of Saul."

cards.question: David decides there's nothing better for him than to escape, so Saul will stop searching all over Israel. Where does he plan to go?

cards.text: So David sets out with his men for Achish son of Maoch, the king of Gath. The LAST time David was in Gath, he pretended to be insane and let his spit run down his beard (1 Samuel 21:13), and now he's moving BACK?!

cards.question: David sets out for Gath with his ___ hundred men.
David and his men settle in Gath with Achish. Each man has his family with him.

cards.text: And David's got his two wives with him: Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail of Carmel, the widow of Nabal. Whole households, friend. This isn't a weekend trip. This is a MOVE.

cards.question: When Saul learns that David has fled to Gath, he keeps searching for him.
Once David's settled in Gath, he goes to King Achish with a request. What does David ask for?

answers.text: A place in one of the outlying towns
A home right inside the royal city
Command over part of the army

cards.question: That day Achish gives David the town of ___.

cards.text: The text says that to this day, Ziklag still belongs to the kings of Judah. And David's time in Philistine territory? A year and four months.
Now David and his men go up and raid the Geshurites, the Girzites and the Amalekites. These people had lived since ancient times in the land stretching to Shur and Egypt.
Whenever David attacks, he leaves no man or woman alive. He takes the flocks and herds, the donkeys, camels and clothing, and heads back to Achish.

cards.question: Back in Gath, Achish asks David, "What have you raided today?" What does David tell him?
David leaves no man or woman alive to be brought to Gath. He says that otherwise they would ___ what he did.
After all of David's reports, Achish starts to suspect that David is lying to him.

cards.text: Achish trusts David, thinking, "Since he has made himself an utter stench to his people Israel, he will be my servant forever." Then the Philistines gather their forces for war against Israel. Uh-oh.

cards.question: With the Philistines gathering for war against Israel, what does Achish tell David?

answers.text: He and his men will go to battle with Achish
He and his men will stay behind and guard Gath
He and his men must leave Philistine land for now

cards.text: And David answers, "Then you will come to know what your servant can do." Friend, I've read that line TEN times, and I still can't tell you whose side it's promising to help.

cards.question: Achish hears David say he'll show what he can do. What does Achish make David?

cards.text: The bodyguard of a Philistine king, with a war against Israel on the way. We'll stop right there, friend, but trust me, this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: The card quotes 1 Samuel 26:25 as "May you be blessed, David my son." The BSB reads "May you be blessed, my son David." The words inside the quotation marks aren't the exact BSB wording. The passage-text script can't catch this because the verse is outside the passage.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included. A paraphrase uses no quotation marks.

findings.problem: Card 11 tells the baker that David raided the Geshurites, the Girzites and the Amalekites, in the land toward Shur. Nothing before card 13 says David hides the truth from Achish. That only comes out on card 14 and in 27:11–12. A thoughtful baker would reason their way to "The land of the Amalekites" or "The towns out near Shur," because those are the places David actually raided. The only way to pick "The Negev of Judah" is to guess that David lied. The setup points the baker away from the right answer.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "undo" doesn't fit the sentence. "They would undo what he did" isn't a believable reason, so the baker can rule it out without knowing the passage. The answers aren't all the same kind of thing.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Too many choice cards can't be reasoned out from the earlier cards. Card 4 (six hundred men) is a number the baker hasn't been given. Card 8 (an outlying town) has no setup about why David would want one. Card 9 (Ziklag) is a name. Card 13 (Negev of Judah) has a setup that points the wrong way. Card 19 (bodyguard for life) is a title. Card 5 is a true or false with no setup. About half of the 11 choice cards are discovery or luck, not a few.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The size of David's band is a minor detail. It doesn't move the passage forward, and the baker doesn't need it to understand the passage. It uses a choice card that could go to a moment that matters, like why David asks to leave the royal city or the custom in 27:11.

rule.text: Ask about the moments that move the passage forward and the details the baker needs to understand it.

findings.problem: Cards 10, 11 and 12 come one after another as plain summaries of 27:6–9, with none of Papa Dorin's voice. There's no reaction, no comparison and no storyteller line. Even 27:6–7, which can hold a laugh (David asking politely to move out of the king's city), is told flat. Across the stop, the humor mostly reads like a nice dad being pleasant, not laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
